methods.name: Peer-Median

methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Electra.aero is a Series B-stage transportation company founded by John Langford that has raised $235M to date. The broader Transportation sector contains eight private peers including Rivian, The Boring Company, and Einride, though no public comparables exist for this frontier subsegment. The narrow peer set—filtered by stage, valuation tier, and business model proximity—lacks sufficient depth (fewer than three datapoints meeting adjacent-stage and similar-scale criteria) to support a reliable peer-median approach.

Consequently, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $235M total raised proxy, reflecting typical Series B step-up dynamics. This method yields an implied valuation of $446M. A conservative sensitivity range anchors the low-end at $380M (15% discount to median) and the high-end at $513M (15% premium to median), accommodating model uncertainty within a ±15% band.

The analysis supports a median valuation of $446M, with a defensible range of $380M to $513M. Key uncertainties stem from the absence of narrow-stage peers and reliance on a single triangulation method. Future validation would benefit from either expanded Transportation peer data at comparable scales or updated internal metrics (burn rate, unit economics, market traction) that could anchor revenue or cash-flow multiples.
